subsystems.name: Dynamic rotor ring
subsystems.role: a cable loop encircling the planet, moving faster than orbital speed so its outward push exceeds gravity and supports everything else.

subsystems.name: Stationary sheath
subsystems.role: a non-orbiting tube or track riding on the rotor by magnetic levitation; because it stands still relative to the ground it acts like fixed land in the sky.

subsystems.name: Magnetic support and power coupling
subsystems.role: transfers force between rotor and sheath, and moves electrical power between them.

subsystems.name: Tethers and ground interface
subsystems.role: cables hanging from the stationary sheath down through the atmosphere, with climbing vehicles, so payloads never need rocket speeds.

subsystems.name: Dynamics and control
subsystems.role: a structure thousands of kilometres long is never rigid, so it must be actively steered and damped.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: collects solar energy and rejects waste heat in vacuum.

subsystems.name: Platforms and industry
subsystems.role: the built-out part: docks, transfer stations, habitats and processing plants on the stationary sheath.

buildSteps.title: Launch the material
buildSteps.detail: Lift thousands of tonnes of cable, magnets and electronics to low Earth orbit with reusable launchers — the ring cannot be launched assembled.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a seed loop
buildSteps.detail: Robots assemble a first partial loop, perhaps a few hundred kilometres of cable, in low orbit.

buildSteps.title: Spin it up
buildSteps.detail: Current is driven through the conductor so it interacts with Earth's magnetic field; the loop is pushed outward and lengthened, trading electrical energy for speed and for a larger radius.

buildSteps.title: Grow to a complete ring
buildSteps.detail: Step by step the loop is expanded until it encircles the planet at a few hundred kilometres altitude, moving at slightly more than orbital velocity — roughly 8 km/s at that height.

buildSteps.title: Add the stationary sheath
buildSteps.detail: A non-orbiting tube is threaded around the moving cable and levitated on it magnetically; the rotor's excess centrifugal force now carries the sheath's weight, and the sheath stops the rotor flying away.

buildSteps.title: Hang the tethers
buildSteps.detail: Cables are lowered from the sheath to the surface. Because the sheath is stationary, these hang under ordinary tension a few hundred kilometres long — no exotic strength needed.

buildSteps.title: Build platforms and stations
buildSteps.detail: Because the sheath stands still, construction is like building on land: docks, habitats, solar arrays, workshops.

buildSteps.title: Duplicate and interconnect
buildSteps.detail: More rings at other inclinations cross the first, creating a global network of fixed transfer points.

prerequisites.why: reusable rockets have cut costs sharply, but the ring needs thousands of tonnes lifted and assembled.
robotic assembly has been demonstrated on a small scale only.
the rotor must carry current and withstand forces over continental distances.

prerequisites.tech: Active control of very large flexible structures
prerequisites.why: control theory exists, but nothing this size has ever been stabilised.
launching every tonne from Earth may be prohibitive; lunar or asteroid material would change the economics.

pathway.milestone: routine reusable launch and small robotic assembly in orbit
pathway.unlocks: the ability to place and join structures in space at falling cost.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrator loop in low orbit spun faster than orbital velocity and held by magnetic support
pathway.unlocks: proof that the dynamic-support principle works outside a paper.

pathway.milestone: an equatorial ring with two or three hanging tethers
pathway.unlocks: routine, low-cost surface-to-orbit transport independent of rockets.

pathway.milestone: in-space manufacturing from lunar or asteroidal material
pathway.unlocks: growth from one ring to many without launching everything from Earth.

pathway.milestone: crossing rings, permanent habitats and orbital industry
pathway.unlocks: the civilisation-scale build-out the concept is aimed at — if the control, materials and cost problems are ever solved.
